41/S0.subgoal: Describe how the Majuli VR tour's design was framed by its objectives and an iterative user-informed process.

41/S1.subgoal: Explain how user categories and 24 information points determined the tour's content scope.

41/S2.subgoal: Describe the starting experience design, including introductory and tutorial videos, a boat ride, and user-group selection.

41/S3.subgoal: Describe how images and videos were preprocessed and ambient sounds were added to improve the visual and auditory experience.

41/S4.subgoal: Describe how the virtual tablet interface provides navigation tools, a video player, and access to information content.

41/S5.subgoal: Explain how minimaps, arrows, and notifications support local orientation, wayfinding, and awareness of cultural videos.

41/S6.subgoal: Describe how island exploration was supported by smooth image transitions and a vehicle-based travel technique.

41/S7.subgoal: Describe how location-relevant videos, textual descriptions, and point-of-interest cues support content exploration.

41/S8.subgoal: Explain how controlled navigation, careful vehicle speed, and consistent visual cues were used to minimize cybersickness.

41/S9.subgoal: Summarize the main points of the lecture.
